speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a skin condition we need to evaluate; please describe the lesion in detail, including its size, color, shape, and how long it has been present. Are there any symptoms like itching, bleeding, or pain associated with it?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text: 62-year-old male with a 30-year smoking history presents with a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the penile shaft and a similar lesion on the left middle finger. Given the chronic nature, failure of previous treatments, and risk factors, do these lesions have irregular borders or have you noticed any bleeding or ulceration? REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_penile_lesion; Biopsy_digital_lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy_penile_lesion: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium. Biopsy_digital_lesion: Cells with nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures within the follicle-bearing epithelium.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma of the penis and digit. The biopsy results showing nuclear hyperchromasia, multinucleation, and increased mitotic figures in the epithelium are diagnostic for malignancy. Given the patient's smoking history and the multifocal nature of the lesions, these findings are consistent with squamous cell carcinoma in both locations.
